summary.headline: S.P. Apparels Q2 FY27 revenue rose 5.8% YoY to ₹452.2 crore, with management guiding to ₹600 crore per quarter in Q3 and Q4.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue was ₹452.2 crore, up 12.8% QoQ and 5.8% YoY, after Q1 was hit by US tariff-related order deferrals. Management said profit growth outpaced revenue, with PAT up 11.9% YoY, and cited improved order visibility, China-plus-one shifts away from Bangladesh, and spare capacity. Sri Lanka, UK and Young Brand Apparel (YBAPL) were the main growth drivers, while the retail business was described as near breakeven at the EBITDA level. The transcript is partly garbled, so some figures (notably the PAT and margin numbers) are uncertain and should be checked against the filing.

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated revenue from operations Q2 FY27
financial_highlights.change: +12.8% QoQ (vs ₹401 crore in Q1); +5.8% YoY (vs ₹427 crore in Q2 FY26)
Profit growth stated to have outpaced revenue growth

financial_highlights.metric: Young Brand Apparel adjusted operational revenue Q2 FY27
UK business (SP UK) Q2 FY27 revenue
financial_highlights.change: More than doubled from ₹18 crore YoY (+111.8%)

financial_highlights.metric: UK business H1 FY27 profit before tax
financial_highlights.change: vs loss of ₹1.5 crore in H1 FY26; profitable for five consecutive quarters

segments.name: Core garments (SPAL India)
segments.commentary: Order book stated at ₹450 crore. Base business YoY softness was attributed by management to a roughly 20% customer contribution loss, with recovery expected from Q3. Capacity utilisation was 74% in Q2, targeted at ~80% near term and 80-85% by end-March.

segments.name: Young Brand Apparel (YBAPL)
segments.commentary: Q2 adjusted operational revenue ₹109.1 crore (+29.4% YoY); order book ₹175 crore. New facilities started in August and are expected to reach full commercial production from next quarter, with capacity targeted at about 1,500 machines by March.

segments.name: SP UK (FPUK London)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ₹38.1 crore, more than doubled YoY, with three new customers added. Order book GBP 4.5 million. Management expects breakeven in Q3 and modest profit in Q4.

segments.name: Sri Lanka operations
segments.commentary: About 1,700 machines; H1 revenue ₹45 crore. FY27 target was cut to ₹150-170 crore from earlier ₹190 crore, with FY28 earlier planned at ₹400 crore. Margins are about 10% due to pre-operative costs in a factory awaiting customer approval. Only 40 machines were operational at the new YBAPL-related setup, with 300 targeted in six months.

segments.name: Retail (Angel & Rocket, Crocodile, online)
segments.commentary: Seven stores (per call) with around ₹70 lakh monthly store revenue; online is around 50% of Angel & Rocket turnover. Retail is about 12-15% of the business, with Crocodile about 87%. Retail is EBITDA positive for about six to seven quarters, with the parent intending to convert secured loans of ₹17 crore to equity this fiscal year.

segments.name: Spinning / yarn
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 spinning revenue close to ₹15 crore; the call framed this as a good performance.

guidance_outlook: Management said revenue should run at about ₹600 crore per quarter in Q3 and Q4 FY27 (management's own statement in response to a question on the ₹2,000 crore FY27 target; the link to that target is unclear from the transcript).
Capacity utilisation expected at about 80% near term and 80-85% by end-March 2027.
Sri Lanka FY27 revenue now seen at ₹150-170 crore (earlier ₹190 crore); FY28 target of about ₹400 crore reiterated.
SP UK expected to reach breakeven in Q3 FY27 and turn profitable in Q4 FY27.
Young Brand Apparel growth guided to at least 20% in FY28, with about 700 machines added from April 2027 in India.
Garment EBITDA margin guidance of about 15%; management also cited a target of 20% for the garments business next year.
risks_watch: Sri Lanka FY27 revenue cut to ₹150-170 crore from ₹190 crore; FY28 ₹400 crore target depends on factory approvals.
Retail still carries higher debt and finance costs; parent needs to convert loans to equity to reduce debt.
Q3 ₹600 crore per quarter run-rate requires a strong pickup in capacity utilisation from 74% to 80-85%.
Garment margins under pressure from loss of duty drawback and Sri Lanka ramp-up costs.
Rupee volatility (around 95 per USD per the call) and 20% open forex exposure.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the H2 recovery and growth outlook, particularly for UK and Young Brand, but cautious on Sri Lanka, where FY27 guidance was trimmed due to delayed customer approvals. Several answers were unclear due to line dropouts, so some numbers should be verified.
key_quotes: We began to see a clear improvement in the second quarter.
Recklessation in the quarter was 74% primarily reflecting the timing of customer orders rather than a lack of available capacity.
Retail is increasingly demonstrating the strength of a more focused operating model. It is no longer a drag on the group.

qa_highlights.question: Why has base business at the Avinashi (core garment) unit not grown YoY, with quarterly volumes falling from about ₹308 crore to about ₹290 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a roughly 20% customer contribution loss, said Q1 and Q2 were affected, and that Q3 onward recovery is under way as the customer has returned, so Q3 and Q4 should be on track.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Sri Lanka machine count and revenue, and is FY27 guidance being cut?
qa_highlights.answer: About 1,700 machines; H1 revenue ₹45 crore, H2 expected ₹70-80 crore, total about ₹150 crore; earlier FY27 plan of ₹190 crore was cut to ₹150-170 crore because one factory awaits customer approval, with FY28 still targeted at ₹400 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the YBAPL capacity ramp, and is Q2 revenue steady-state?
qa_highlights.answer: Only 40 machines operational so far, started in August; 80 machines by mid-January, 200 after three months and 300 within six months; total capacity about 1,500 machines by March; H2 expected similar to H1.

qa_highlights.question: Why did garment margins decline YoY and what is the margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Loss of duty drawback of about 6.5% and Sri Lanka's pre-operative costs (about 10% margin) pulled margins down; guidance is about 15% EBITDA margin, with Sri Lanka expected to improve in two to three months and a 20% target for next year.

qa_highlights.question: What are the plans and funding needs for the retail business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said retail is EBITDA positive for six to seven quarters; the parent has secured loans of ₹17 crore that may be converted to equity this financial year; debt has risen and a PBT-positive run for three more quarters precedes possible external fundraising.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 2,000 crore FY27 revenue target status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said revenue should run at about ₹600 crore per quarter in Q3 and Q4 FY27.

capex_capacity: Core garments (SPAL India) capacity utilisation was 74% in Q2 FY27; management expects about 80% in the near term and 80-85% by end-March 2027, and says the 74% reflected order timing rather than lack of capacity.
Customers approved an additional factory/capacity in India; utilisation of that capacity expected to improve. Management is evaluating one or two more factories as part of the next growth phase.

Young Brand Apparel (YBAPL): new facilities started in August; ~40 machines operational at the time of the call, targeted at 80 machines by mid-January, 200 after three months and 300 within six months. Total YBAPL capacity expected at about 1,500 machines by March 2027. Management said the new facilities should reach full commercial production from next quarter.
Around 700 machines to be added in India from April 2027 by regaining ~1,000 machines previously reduced at the same factory (as stated on the call).

Sri Lanka: about 1,700 machines; one of four factories is awaiting customer approval, expected within three to four months (one analyst answer said before end-March); the factory is being run on job work in the meantime. Management expects to reach close to ₹400 crore in Sri Lanka in FY28 with four factories, and is considering one more Sri Lanka setup for YBAPL.
Management said it will ensure four Sri Lanka factories are settled (materials, utilisation, quality, delivery) by end-March, and then consider one or two more factories.
Retail: seven Angel & Rocket stores (per call) with ~₹70 lakh monthly store revenue; plan to open four more stores and reach 20-25 standalone stores by end-2028.
demand_pricing: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue ₹452.2 crore (+12.8% QoQ, +5.8% YoY); management attributed Q1 weakness to US tariff uncertainty causing order deferrals, and said US customers have since confirmed orders.
Core garments order book stated at ₹450 crore; management said base business softness reflected a roughly 20% customer contribution loss, with recovery expected from Q3 FY27.
YBAPL Q2 adjusted operational revenue ₹109.1 crore (+29.4% YoY); order book ₹175 crore; growth guided at at least 20% in FY28 driven by Salem expansion.

UK (SP UK/FPUK London) Q2 revenue ₹38.1 crore (+111.8% YoY from ₹18 crore), H1 revenue ₹71 crore vs ₹30 crore; order book GBP 4.5 million; three new customers added and more UK retailers in discussion.

Sri Lanka H1 FY27 revenue ₹45 crore; H2 expected ₹70-80 crore; FY27 now ₹150-170 crore vs earlier ₹190 crore; margins about 10% due to pre-operative costs. Garment margin guidance about 15% EBITDA, with a 20% target cited for next year.
Management said revenue should be about ₹600 crore per quarter in Q3 and Q4 FY27 in reply to a question on the ₹2,000 crore FY27 target.

Competition: customers are diversifying sourcing away from Bangladesh (China plus one); management said India and Sri Lanka are at par with Bangladesh on landed cost post-FTA for basic/volume products, but Bangladesh remains stronger for high-volume basic products on efficiency. Management said it is at a level playing field for fashion products.
Margin pressure: loss of duty drawback (about 6.5%) and Sri Lanka ramp-up costs weighed on garment margins YoY.

Retail: about 12-15% of group business, Crocodile about 87%; online about 50% of Angel & Rocket turnover; online growing 200-300% a year; EBITDA positive for six to seven quarters; ~₹40 crore retail revenue expected in the next two years per one answer.
Spinning H1 FY27 revenue close to ₹15 crore.
SPAL Kids/Sri Lanka: management said SQK business expects 50-100% growth over two to three years, with a target of ₹500 crore in three to five years; M&S among new customers.
Currency: rupee around 95 per USD; about 80% of exposure hedged after order confirmation, leaving 20% open. Cotton inventory held for 45-60 days (range 30-90 days).

growth.why: Management says revenue should run about ₹600 crore per quarter in Q3 and Q4 (consistent with the held ₹2,000 crore FY27 target), backed by a ₹450 crore core order book, a ₹175 crore YBAPL order book, a GBP 4.5m UK order book, and YBAPL capacity rising to ~1,500 machines by March 2027, though the link from the Q3/Q4 run-rate to the ₹2,000 crore target is unclear and Sri Lanka FY27 was cut to ₹150-

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Garment EBITDA guided at about 15%, with Sri Lanka margins (about 10%) expected to improve as pre-operative costs fall over two to three months and a 20% garment margin target cited for next year, though loss of ~6.5% duty drawback is a headwind.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: YBAPL new facilities started in August, targeting 80 machines by mid-January, 300 within six months and about 1,500 total by March 2027; about 700 machines added in India from April 2027 and Sri Lanka's fourth factory awaits approval within 3-4 months.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Core order book is ₹450 crore with recovery from Q3, YBAPL order book is ₹175 crore with 20%+ growth guided for FY28, UK order book is GBP 4.5 million, and Sri Lanka H2 is expected at ₹70-80 crore versus ₹45 crore in H1.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is only 74% in Q2 (target 80-85% by March 2027), so there is no immediate capacity shortfall, but management is evaluating one or two more factories for the next growth phase.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held the ₹2,000 crore FY27 target and cut Sri Lanka guidance, and H1 consolidated revenue is only about ₹853 crore (₹401 crore Q1 plus ₹452 crore Q2), so an upgrade would need a steep H2 ramp.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Sri Lanka FY27 was already cut to ₹150-170 crore from ₹190 crore, and the ₹600 crore per quarter run-rate for Q3/Q4 needs utilisation to rise from 74% to 80-85%, with the Avinashi base business still down after losing ~20% of a customer's contribution.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Retail plans four more Angel & Rocket stores (seven today) toward 20-25 standalone stores by end-2028, and SPAL Kids/SQK targets ₹500 crore in three to five years with M&S among new customers, but no dated product launches were given.

rows.label: SP UK breakeven in Q3 and profit in Q4 FY27
rows.why: UK revenue more than doubled to ₹38.1 crore in Q2 (+111.8% YoY), H1 PBT was ₹0.5 crore versus a ₹1.5 crore loss, and the GBP 4.5 million order book supports management's breakeven and profit guidance.

rows.label: Conversion of ₹17 crore secured loans to equity
rows.why: Management intends to convert the parent's secured loans of ₹17 crore to equity to cut retail debt, but timing and approval are not firm.

rows.label: US customers confirmed orders after Q1 tariff deferrals
rows.why: Q1 revenue was ₹401 crore after tariff-related deferrals, and management said US customers have since confirmed orders alongside the ₹450 crore core order book.

tone.note: Management was confident on the H2 recovery, UK and YBAPL growth, but cautious on Sri Lanka, whose FY27 guidance was cut on delayed customer approvals.
